# Exact versions the checks are known to pass with.
#
#     pip install -r tools/requirements.txt -c tools/constraints.txt
#
# requirements.txt says what is needed and stays readable; this file says which build was
# verified. The distinction matters here more than in most repositories: check_all.py
# compares generated files byte for byte, so a serializer that changes its whitespace or
# its ordering makes a derived file look stale when nothing about the ontology moved. Left
# unpinned, an upstream release could turn CI red for a reason that has nothing to do with
# the change under review.
#
# To move to newer versions: bump them here, regenerate, and commit the result. If a
# derived file changes, that is the serializer talking, and it belongs in its own commit.
rdflib==7.1.3
pyparsing==3.1.1
openpyxl==3.1.5
et-xmlfile==1.1.0
pyoxigraph==0.5.9
pyshacl==0.30.0
owlready2==0.47
